exposure: high-dose oxytocin regimen (starting dose 5 mU/min with 5 mU/min increments every 30 minutes)
low-dose oxytocin regimen (starting dose 2.5 mU/min with 2.5 mU/min increments every 30 minutes)
cohort: 100 term pregnant women requiring labour augmentation were enrolled.
finding: High-dose oxytocin for labour augmentation is associated with better cervical ripening, a shorter induction-to-delivery interval, and a higher rate of successful vaginal delivery without increasing maternal or neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: The high-dose oxytocin group had significantly lower caesarean section rates (28% vs 46%) and a higher rate of successful vaginal delivery compared to the low-dose group.
birth_weight: Assessed as an outcome; participants were term pregnant women.
gest_age: Participants were term pregnant women; gestational age was assessed as a baseline parameter and was similar between groups.
